scheme_name: Scheme for Rearing Purebreed Gir/ Kankarage Male Cow Calves with Excellent Genetic Quality
description:
The Scheme for Rearing Purebreed Gir/Kankarage Male Cow Calves with Excellent Genetic Quality was launched by the Government of India in 2014. 

This scheme aims to enhance the productivity of the dairy sector in India by promoting the breeding of high-quality Gir and Kankarage male calves. 

The Gir breed is known for its high milk production and adaptability to various climatic conditions. 

Kankarage is another indigenous breed that is recognized for its resilience and productivity. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to improve the genetic quality of cattle in India. 

The government aims to increase the population of purebred Gir and Kankarage cattle by providing financial assistance to farmers. 

The scheme targets an increase in milk production by at least 20% over the next five years. 

Farmers participating in this scheme can receive financial support of up to ₹30,000 per calf. 

This financial assistance is intended to cover the costs of feeding, veterinary care, and other necessary expenses. 

The scheme also aims to promote the use of artificial insemination to improve the genetic quality of cattle. 

By 2025, the government aims to have at least 50,000 purebred Gir and Kankarage calves reared under this scheme. 

The eligibility criteria for farmers include owning a minimum of two acres of agricultural land. 

Farmers must also have a basic understanding of cattle rearing and management practices. 

The age limit for farmers applying for this scheme is between 18 to 60 years. 

Income criteria stipulate that the annual income of the farmer should not exceed ₹2 lakh. 

Farmers must also possess a valid Aadhaar card and land ownership documents. 

The application process involves several steps. 

First, interested farmers must visit their local Animal Husbandry Department office. 

They need to fill out the application form provided at the office. 

The form requires details such as the farmer's name, address, land ownership details, and the number of calves to be reared. 

Farmers must submit the application along with required documents. 

These documents include a copy of the Aadhaar card, land ownership documents, and a passport-sized photograph. 

Once the application is submitted, it will be reviewed by the local Animal Husbandry officer. 

The officer will conduct an inspection of the farm to verify the details provided in the application. 

If approved, the farmer will receive the financial assistance directly into their bank account. 

The disbursement of funds typically occurs within 30 days of approval. 

The scheme also includes provisions for regular monitoring and evaluation of the rearing process. 

Farmers are required to maintain records of the calves reared under this scheme. 

They must provide updates on the health and growth of the calves to the Animal Husbandry Department. 

The government conducts periodic training programs for farmers to enhance their skills in cattle management. 

These training programs cover topics such as feeding practices, health care, and breeding techniques. 

The scheme is implemented by the Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying under the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

Farmers can contact the local Animal Husbandry Department for more information. 

The contact details for the department can be found on the official website of the Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying. 

The scheme has been positively received by farmers in various states. 

Many farmers have reported an increase in milk production and income as a result of participating in this scheme. 

The government has allocated ₹100 crore for the implementation of this scheme in the current financial year. 

This funding is expected to support the rearing of approximately 33,000 calves. 

The scheme is part of a broader initiative to promote indigenous breeds of cattle in India. 

The government recognizes the importance of preserving genetic diversity in livestock. 

By promoting the rearing of purebred Gir and Kankarage cattle, the scheme aims to contribute to sustainable agriculture. 

The scheme also aligns with the National Livestock Mission, which focuses on enhancing livestock productivity. 

Farmers are encouraged to adopt best practices in cattle rearing to maximize the benefits of the scheme. 

The government provides additional resources such as veterinary services and access to quality feed. 

Farmers can also benefit from the establishment of cooperatives to enhance their bargaining power. 

The scheme is expected to create employment opportunities in rural areas. 

It aims to empower farmers by providing them with the necessary resources and knowledge. 

The government plans to expand the scheme to include more indigenous breeds in the future. 

This expansion will further enhance the genetic quality of livestock in India. 

The success of the scheme will be measured by the increase in the population of purebred cattle and overall milk production. 

Regular assessments will be conducted to evaluate the impact of the scheme on farmers' livelihoods. 

The scheme is a significant step towards achieving self-sufficiency in milk production in India. 

It aims to reduce the dependency on imported dairy products. 

The government encourages farmers to participate actively in the scheme for better outcomes. 

Overall, the Scheme for Rearing Purebreed Gir/Kankarage Male Cow Calves with Excellent Genetic Quality represents a comprehensive approach to improving the dairy sector in India. 

It combines financial assistance with training and support to ensure the successful rearing of high-quality cattle. 

The initiative is expected to have long-term benefits for farmers and the dairy industry as a whole. 

By focusing on indigenous breeds, the scheme also contributes to the conservation of India's rich livestock heritage. 

Farmers are urged to take advantage of this scheme to enhance their livelihoods and contribute to the nation's dairy production goals.
